The answer to your question is that the proportion of thin 0-1 mm melanomas presenting in South West England has significantly increased from 2003 to 2012, while there is no significant change in the thick>4 mm melanomas. This may be a result of increased public awareness due to effective public health campaigns which has significant prognostic and financial implications.

This increase in thin melanomas suggests that public awareness campaigns have contributed to an earlier detection of these skin cancer cases. The same campaigns are likely responsible for the observed decrease in thick>4 mm melanomas, as people may be more likely to seek medical attention if they have a thinner lesion.
